statement: The Mongol invasion of Hungary (1241) under Batu Khan and Subutai destroyed approximately 20–50% of Hungary's population through battle, massacre, and famine. King Béla IV fled to a Dalmatian island; the Mongols occupied the Hungarian plain. Only news of Ögedei Khan's death (1241) caused the Mongol withdrawal in spring 1242. Béla IV spent the remainder of his reign rebuilding Hungary: granting noble privileges, building stone castles, settling Cumans and other nomadic peoples as military colonists. The rebuilt Hungary successfully resisted a second Mongol invasion (1285).
